utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. The proceedings this afternoon will go on with the two of us present under Rule 15 bis. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. As you can see, Mr. Milan Simic is not present. I've had a conversation with Ms. Baen who instructs me that the Defence for Milan Simic is in a position to stipulate or agree that this witness would be in a position to identify him if he were here. I think that Ms. Baen can agree with that assertion.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, while we are on the issue of Mr. Milan Simic, can you tell the Chamber how long you've known him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him from about town. I know him as someone who worked in the Buducnost factory. I also know him and used to see him in certain restaurants.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Approximately how long have you known him, or perhaps I should say had you known him, as of April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the past five years, I knew him pretty well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I understand from your answer that you mean in the five years preceding April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what sort of contacts did you have with him? Were they mainly social, mainly professional, or just meetings from time to time in the street? What sort of contact, in other words?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Accidental meetings in the street or a restaurant perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can I ask you to turn your attention again to the days following the events of the 16th and 17th of April? On Friday, you described some events that you observed on the day of the 17th. I want you now to turn your attention to the day of the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, 1992, in the morning, looking from my house, I saw a military vehicle surrounded by soldiers of the Yugoslav People's Army, Djuheric, nicknamed Coc, walked in front of the vehicle. He was dressed in a military uniform, and he was a carrying a megaphone, and he was calling out to citizens to surrender their arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Just some details about this sight that you saw. First of all, the soldiers that you've referred to, and I'm not talking about the man Djuheric but the soldiers that you saw, can you comments on whether or not they were locals or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These soldiers were not local.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How were they dressed? Did they have any similarities to the camouflaged men that you had seen the day before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were wearing uniforms of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this man Djuheric, of what ethnic background was he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djuheric is an ethnic Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was he a local resident, that is, a man from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a local of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you have any idea if he was a member of any military organisation or group in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is common knowledge in Samac that he was a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, you say that he was calling out to the citizens to surrender their arms. Was that call to surrender having any effect? Were people in fact surrendering arms or responding to his calls?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see that. I couldn't see anyone turning over their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you remain at home throughout the day, that is, the day of the 18th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed inside the whole day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: With your family?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my family, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Other than the sight of this Djuheric fellow and the soldiers who accompanied him, did you see any other military activity throughout the day that you can recall? If not, just say so.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any other military activity. All I can say is that on that, or the following day, the military vehicle reappeared, but that was a military truck carrying troops. It drove along the streets of the town and, again, through a megaphone, they were calling out to people to surrender weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do I take it from your answer, therefore, that in the few days after the 16th -- the events of the 16th and 17th of April, there were several calls on the citizenry to surrender their weapons, using these trucks and megaphones and so on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In those few days, did you have occasion to listen to the radio in order to try and get some information as to what was going on, what was happening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I listened to the radio in those days. The radio station was renamed. At that time, it was called Bosanski Samac Radio before, and then it was renamed to the Serbian Samac Radio station. I also heard an appeal to all men to report to the headquarters of the Territorial Defence to be registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And was that a call directed to all men regardless of ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you respond to that call?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not want to serve the forces occupying my town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, just answer the next question, if you can, with a yes or a no. I want to establish a time frame. Were you eventually arrested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What day were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 22nd of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks. Let's use that as a fixing point. In relation to the 22nd of April, 1992, when would you say that the call to report to the TO occurred? If you can't say precisely, let us know. But if you can give us an idea, please do.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The call was issued on the 19th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you or your family make any attempt to get out of Bosanski Samac or alternatively obtain information about getting out of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother tried to get a permit for his family and my family to leave the town. He approached -- he had approached the newly appointed chief of police, Stevan Todorovic with this request and was denied. He was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters' correction. I was told that a permit should be sought from Perica Krstanovic, who was my neighbour. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who told you to approach Perica Krstanovic and why were you -- was any reason given why you should approach him in particular?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a neighbour of mine and I had asked him at one point if there was a possibility for me and my family to leave the town, and he said it was possible only with the permission from the new authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And was your obtaining of that information that caused your brother to approach Todorovic with a view to getting permission to get out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your brother report to you on Todorovic's response?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He came to my home and told me, "I had been to see the new chief of police Stevan Todorovic and I had tried to get a permit for our two families to leave, but he refused me, and he ordered me to go and fetch you and said that we should both come and see him."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I take it at this stage you had no idea of what awaited you should you respond to such a call?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: We'll get on to what did await you shortly, but before we do that, I'd like to ask you if in the time leading up to your arrest, if you saw anyone with white armbands?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see people with white armbands. My father himself came to our place wearing such an armband, and he brought several more, and he said that Marko Kuresevic had been going from apartment to apartment in his residential building, distributing white armbands, and he said he had told people that they could go out into the street only with a white armband on their left arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: First of all, the ethnic background of this gentleman, Marko Kuresevic, what is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is an ethnic Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your father provide a report or tell you of any official reason as to why white armbands should be worn?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see any of the citizenry wearing white armbands in the period of time before your arrest?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the window of my house, I saw several people walking by in the street wearing such armbands on their sleeves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what ethnic background were they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see any citizens not wearing white armbands?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were citizens of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And these observations, were they made from your home, from inside your house, looking out into the street and so on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like you now to turn your attention to the day of your arrest, the 22nd of April, and we will go into that in a little more detail. Can you explain to the Chamber, please, how it came about that you attended at the police -- at the SUP? Perhaps I'm leading you there and I shouldn't be, but did you in fact go to the SUP as part of your -- as part of your being arrested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning of the 22nd, my wife told me that a friend was asking for me on the phone. When I took the receiver, I recognised the voice of Stevan Todorovic, who told me that I was to come to the SUP immediately for an interview concerning my employer, my company, and if I don't come myself, he would send a police car to fetch me. I did not want to allow a police car to come anywhere near our house. I didn't want my children to see any such thing so I went. When I entered the building of the SUP, Todorovic was in a room. The door was ajar. He saw me entering and he beckoned me to come in. When I entered the room, there was another civilian besides Todorovic, and a couple of soldiers. Todorovic was wearing a black uniform, which I hadn't seen before. He motioned me to stand in the middle of the room, and he told me, "The Serbs had a premonition of what was going to happen, and they took action. From now on, this is a Serbian town." I didn't say anything to that. So he asked me whether I was a member of the SDA. I said I wasn't. Then he asked me if I knew anything about the allocation of money by my company for the purchase of weapons for the SDA. I said I didn't know anything about it and I didn't believe it was true. Then he asked me, "Has there been any shooting from your house?" I answered, "There has been no shooting, not only from my house but from my street, at all." Then he motioned a guard to take me away, but I asked him for permission to make a brief phone call to my home. I was allowed to do that. I told my wife that I won't be home for a while. And after that, the guard escorted me to the premises of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: From your answer, something must have happened that made you aware that you were going to be locked up, incarcerated. Did -- were you told by Todorovic that in fact you were to be arrested and incarcerated, before seeking permission to make the phone call to your wife? Otherwise there wouldn't have been any need to do that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said, "We will lock you up until we've had a chance to check Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. all this."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So you managed to speak to your wife. And were you then taken to the TO across the road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Again, before I ask you about events in the TO, I'd like the Chamber to have a time frame. How long did you remain in the TO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained inside the TO building from the 22nd to the 29th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you then taken somewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken then together with the others, to the military barracks in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's look at that week that you were in custody at the TO. I'd like you to describe what you saw when you were first taken into the TO and your eyes adjusted and could you see around yourself. Tell the Chamber, give the Chamber a description of what you saw.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I entered that room, which was sized about five by five metres, it had a concrete floor. The first thing that struck me was that there was a lot of human hair and there was blood on the floor. There were about 40 people inside. Some of them had swollen faces and wounds on their bodies. Their faces were blue. They had open wounds on their heads. Blood had dried on their skin and faces. The walls were also covered with bloodstains and dried blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Could you smell anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It smelled of blood, of dried blood, and the stench was awful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In the period of a week or so that -- of a week during which you remained in the TO, did you see men beaten?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened on a daily basis. Most often in the afternoon hours or at night. Every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to enable the Chamber to have a general picture of these beatings and then I might direct you to one or two specific occasions. Firstly, the frequency. You've commented already that it happened every day, mostly in the afternoon. Can you comment on the numbers of men who would be beaten in the afternoons? Are you talking about one or two victims here, or three or four, or did it vary?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It varied. Ten to 15 people would be beaten every day. When people were taken out, they would always beg not to be taken out because their wounds had not healed yet, the wounds from the previous beating.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell the Chamber or comment on the -- whether or not instruments were used in administering these beatings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They used all kinds of things, rifle butts, barrels, wooden sticks, metal sticks, they kicked people with boots.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you comment on the intensity or ferocity of the beatings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beatings were so intense that new wounds would be inflicted with every blow and there would be blood spraying everywhere. People would come back after the beatings all covered in blood. You could see those open, gaping wounds. You could see the flesh, the skin and the flesh on their faces and on their hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who was carrying out these beatings? And by that, if you can give us some names, by all means do, but I'm also interested in the position of -- and what groups the people who were carrying out the beatings belonged to, soldiers, policemen, civilians, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time the beatings were administered by the specials from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did anyone other than these specials engage in beating men in that first week in which you were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber if any of the men who engaged in carrying out the beatings appeared to have been drinking?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to ask you now about some specific episodes during that week. I'm sorry, I should withdraw that question. Before I do, before I get on to specific episodes, I'd like to ask you about another aspect of what you saw and that's this: Did you see or hear any singing going on in the TO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They forced us to sing Chetnik songs. On some occasions we had to do that for hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did any of the men fall down or collapse from this being forced to stand and sing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally, there were people who collapsed. They fainted. And those standing next to them would assist them to their feet and help them to stand, because if somebody was found not to be standing up while they had to sing, it would mean additional torture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you give the Chamber an idea of just how loud the noise was coming from the TO and how far, in your estimation it would have carried? And I'm referring to the TO -- the singing in the TO, and in addition, to the screams and yells of the men as they were beaten.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had to sing very loudly. I think the range would be at least half a kilometre. You could hear our singing at a distance of at least a half a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you about specific beatings and attacks that you saw during that week. Do you know of a man nicknamed, I think, Dikan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a small, elderly man, aged between 60 and 65, a member of the Special Forces got in one day, asked for Dikan. The old man said that it was him. He took him and slammed him against the concrete and continued hitting him with a wooden 2 by 4. The old man moaned and begged to be let go, and he was saying, "You're going to kill me." But this member of the Special Forces kept on hitting him. At one point I saw the old man fall over what -- a Jerry can for water. His body remained motionless and there was blood gushing out of his mouth. This member of the Special Forces dragged him out. And then we heard a shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was the name of the man from the Special Forces, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Lugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you say he was dragged out, was that -- does that mean he was dragged out into the courtyard of the TO and shot there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was dragged out into the courtyard. He was dragged in front of the room in which we were sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was the door open?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The door was ajar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how many times was he shot, can you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One or two shots. There were one or two shots. I can't recall with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did this man, Lugar, say anything after he'd murdered Dikan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard him shout, "Throw the dog into the Sava River."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did any of the representatives of the new Serb state come along and investigate this crime, as far as you're aware, take statements from you, any police officers try and find out what had happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one asked for any statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What about the good chief of police? Did he come over and speak to the prisoners and ask what had happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You know a gentleman named Sead Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what was his occupation prior to the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the regular police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And his ethnic background, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what was the ethnic background of your fellow prisoners in the TO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were they all local Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were any of them combatants dressed in military fatigues or report to you or report to others, fellow prisoners, that they'd been arrested as combatants or fighting?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm going to object --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm objecting to the term "combatant" because it calls for a legal conclusion, only because under international law, some of the case law, under the case law, combatant is a legal term that the judges are supposed to decide. So I object to legal conclusion. I think that counsel can ask the questions about what he asked later in the question, about arms and this, that and the other, but the term "combatant" is something that Your Honours have to decide. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, I'm sure you can rephrase the question and use ordinary terms. MR. DI FAZIO: Would "soldier" be okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because a soldier is not necessarily a combatant in the terms we use in the Tribunal. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were any of these men that you saw in the TO dressed as soldiers or did you hear them report that they'd been arrested while carrying out the sort of activities soldiers carry out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the room, there were only civilians. No one had been arrested as a soldier. No one had been arrested while in combat, while fighting. They had all been brought in from their homes. That's where they had been arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks. Now, what about this man Sead Mujkanovic, I'd like to know if you saw him physically attacked during that week in which you were in the TO.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was beaten quite often, but I will never forget that one occasion where a member of the Special Forces came in, told him to open his mouth, pushed in the rifle barrel, told him to close his mouth, and pulled out the barrel, and with the sights on the barrel, broke some of his teeth. Then he told him, "Spit out." To make sure that he had managed to knock out some of his teeth, and to actually see how many of his teeth he managed to knock out in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. In the time that you were incarcerated in the TO in this week leading up to the 29th, were you ever taken out of the TO building, taken elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where did you get your meals?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got our meals in the Utva factory, which is about 1 kilometre away from the TO building. This was for all the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Presumably, then, you had to be taken out of the TO and taken down to the Utva factory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were taken there by truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this is the episode I'm interested in. You say you were taken down by truck. Were you under armed guard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the truck that I was in was at the end of the column and I saw a vehicle driving behind us with about four people in the vehicle. They were armed and in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You say in the truck that you were in, are you implying that the prisoners were transported in more than one truck?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: About how many truck loads of prisoners went down to the Utva factory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No response]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises, we did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can the -- maybe you can repeat the question and then the witness can answer. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: There was a little problem with the interpreting or the interpreters hearing your answer there. My question was: How many truckloads of prisoners actually went down to the Utva factory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No response]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Again, we did not hear the answer because of the -- perhaps because of the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be asked to sit nearer the microphone and also can the witness please speak up? MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Speak up nice and clearly, Mr. Delic. We know that you've answered but obviously it wasn't carrying very clearly. Tell us how many trucks. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks. And where in the Utva factory did the prisoners congregate for their lunch?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were taken to the canteen of the Utva factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: On this occasion, did you see any of the defendants there? Just answer me yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How far away from you was he when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same distance as here in this courtroom, between myself and him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And at the time that you saw him, were you surrounded by your fellow prisoners or in company with your fellow prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was with other prisoners, and he was facing us. So that he was able to see all of us. He stood there with a group of maybe two or three men. They were all dressed in the uniforms of the Yugoslav People's Army, just as he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Just answer yes or no. Did you -- did you look at him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he look at you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber what he would have seen when he looked at you? A.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Objection, speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think you can rephrase your question. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well. Thank you. I can put the -- attain my objective this way, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you described to the Chamber the appearance of your fellow prisoners in detail, please, every single detail, clothing, faces, bodies and so on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some people had great difficulty walking. People had wounds on their heads, on their faces. Most of them had dark blue faces because of the torture they had undergone, they had blood on their hair, on their clothes. Open lacerations on their faces and hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What about their clothing? Were they dressed in ordinary civilian clothes, first of all? And secondly, was there any blood or dried blood on their clothing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all in civilian clothes, with dried blood on their clothes, and because of the beatings they had undergone, there were holes and tears on their clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You described some of the people not being able to walk properly. Can you remember any of the names of the people who couldn't walk properly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember [redacted]as we left the TO building to go to the truck, towards the trucks, the police officers standing around this area would beat people as they walked towards the truck, and as [redacted] managed to reach the truck with great difficulty, he was unable to get on the truck. I helped him, risking a beating or even to be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you were at the Utva factory waiting for lunch, was he in a position to be able to stand up by himself or did he need assistance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was unable to stand up by himself. One or two prisoners had to help him stand up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did you remain at the Utva factory having your lunch?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you recall how long Blagoje Simic was there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he greet any of the prisoners or speak to them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't greet anyone. He did not speak to anyone. He looked at us as if he had never seen us in his life.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In the time that you were in the TO building, up until the 29th, when you were moved to Brcko, were you personally beaten?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Have you got any idea how it was that you escaped or any reason why it was that you should have escaped a beating?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took people to beat them up in the courtyard. As they did that, the members of the Special Forces would come to the room with a piece of paper from which they would read out the names or nicknames of persons in the room. They got those names from someone, because it was impossible for them to know these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I take it, then, that you've got no idea why it is that you personally escaped beating at the hands of these men?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know a man named Omer Nalic and another man named Hasan Bicic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were they ever taken out of the TO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear all of the interpretation. Could it be repeated?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Were those two gentlemen ever taken out of the TO building for any reason in that week that you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What -- when were they taken out and what was your understanding of the reason that they were taken out of the TO building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people that they assumed had foreign exchange or other valuables at home, the system in place was to beat such people for -- or torture such people for a few days in a row and when they saw that that person was at the end of his tether, that he was at the edge of death, they would come in and they would put this large key to the entrance gate into that person's mouth. They would turn it and ask the person whether he was willing to buy his life. And then they took them to their homes and asked them to hand over the foreign exchange or other valuables.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What I'd like to know is this: Is this something that was reported to you or did you actually see these --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just let's be sure about this. Let me finish my question first. Did you actually see the key being shoved into the man's throat and the demand being made or is it something that was reported to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told after these people returned that they had been taken to their homes, and they themselves opened their mouths to show me the wounds that the turning of the key had left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've mentioned that on the 29th of April, you moved to Brcko. I'd like you to briefly describe to the Chamber who went with you to Brcko. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from three prisoners, we were all transferred to Brcko, all of us who had been in the TO building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you recall who were the three who were left behind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that Izet Izetbegovic was left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You can't remember who the other two were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks. And where were you taken to in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took us to the barracks of the Yugoslav People's Army in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Again, give the Chamber a time frame on the period of time you spent in Brcko. How long were you there? And were you eventually transferred from there? And if so, where were you transferred to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Brcko, we were locked up in the prison of the barracks until the 2nd of May, 1992. And then we were transferred to the barracks in Bijeljina. That is also a JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. Were you mistreated whilst you were in Brcko or did you -- and did you see anyone else being mistreated? By that I mean beaten or assaulted and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrive at the barracks, the soldiers pulled us off the trucks, searched us and tied our hands behind our backs with wire. We remained with our hands tied behind our backs in this way until the next morning. It was in this interval that they brought a man whom we called "Zuti" and military policemen beat him for several hours. I remember the moment when they threw him in prison. The policeman who was holding a military truncheon, which is twice as thick and big as the police truncheon, beat this prisoner until the truncheon split in two. When he was thrown in, he fell to a spot right beside me, and he told me, "I don't know why they are beating me. I was just a watchman in my company. I was crossing the street to get some coffee and I had in my hand a cell phone and they accused me of owning a remote control radio transmitter and that I was a spy. Whereas in actual fact, I'm a manual worker."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was the ethnic background of this man and where was he from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Muslim from Brcko. After a while, they brought another two young men, the Stjepanovic brothers, Andrija and Andzelko. For the entire day, they beat them outside on the other side of the metal bars behind which we were standing. And they only made brief pauses to show them some sort of statement. They would take a brief look at the statement and then they would continue to be beaten. There was a large machine-gun pointing at us, and they said, "If anyone tries anything, if anyone moves, we will shoot." At all times, there were one or two policemen next to that machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Civilian police or military police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber whether or not all the men from Bosanski Samac were held in the one place at the barracks in Brcko or whether they were placed in separate rooms, separate cells?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the prison cells were smaller, we were divided among several cells.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said that you moved to -- you were transferred -- I'm sorry, I'll withdraw that question. I have one more question about Brcko. Do you -- do you have any idea as to the reason why you were transferred from Bosanski Samac to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Objection, speculation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Never mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I don't think that was asking the witness to speculate. He could have known as a fact. He could have been told.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I said, "Never mind," Judge, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's get back to the move to Bijeljina. Again, was it most of the Bosanski Samac prisoners who were transferred with you to the barracks in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the prisoners, the entire group, were transferred as a group from Brcko to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you accompanied by any men who were not from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were all of them -- I'll withdraw that question. Was any of them mentally retarded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While we were in Brcko, a man was thrown into my cell, aged perhaps around 50, who was beaten up, but when we tried to talk to him, we noticed that he is not of sound mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And was he -- was he transferred to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was transferred together with us to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Anything happen to him in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in the courtyard of the barracks in Bijeljina and started to get off, at one point, when a certain number of us had already gotten out, a gunshot was heard. We continued to disembark, and I noticed that a group of soldiers was trying to prevent one soldier from doing something, and it seemed to me that he -- this soldier wanted to continue shooting at us. I passed by a man who was lying on the ground. Blood was still flowing from his wound, and I recognised that retarded old man who was together with us in Brcko. He had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long did you remain in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We remained in Bijeljina until the middle of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In that time, leading up to the middle of May, whilst you were in Bijeljina, were you mistreated at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spent our first day there on the premises of the barracks, before being transferred to the gym of the barracks. As soon as we got there, they ordered us to kneel along the wall facing the wall directly but without touching it. And that went on for hours. Soldiers walked behind us, along this line, and beat people on the head or elsewhere on the body at random, and they would always say, "And what have you done?" Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Several days later, one evening, soldiers took me out of that gym and on the way, they told me that I stank. We arrived in a bathroom. They turned on a cold shower and left me under it for half an hour, whereas they kept -- they stood by laughing. They asked me if I was cold? And I could hear them, only hear them sharpening their knives, using some sort of object that I couldn't see. But they were leering and laughing, and after this, I was told -- or I was taken back to the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you clothed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took that shower completely naked. I just picked up my clothes, went to the gym and got dressed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, what I want to know is did they force to you take your clothes off?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did they force you to get into the shower?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was the water cold?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an icy shower.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How did you feel after that experience?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shivering with cold, and felt very, very humiliated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that some of the soldiers finally made an inquiry as to what you had done. In the time that you were in Bijeljina, were you interrogated or asked questions by anyone that gave you any insight or idea as to why it was that you were incarcerated and locked up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was interrogated by a military man. He conducted the questioning in that gym, calling out individual names. When I came up to him, he asked about my name and surname. He asked me why I had been arrested. And I replied how I was arrested and quoted the reasons that had been given me at the Bosanski Samac SUP. Then he asked if I had been arrested as a civilian? And I answered affirmatively. He took my papers, inspected them, and then he told me, "Mistakes happen in wartime. You will be released soon."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you say you quoted the reasons that had been given to you at the Bosanski Samac SUP, are you referring to what Todorovic had told you, namely the purchase of weapons through your company and shooting from your building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I told him about all the questions that Todorovic had asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you called upon to sign anything, sign a statement or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you recall the date from when you were taken away from Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 13th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were all of the Bosanski Samac prisoners taken back to Bosanski Samac or were some of them taken elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not. We heard a helicopter landing in the compound of the barracks in Bijeljina, and after that, several people were taken away in that helicopter. We were told that they were flying to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know Sulejman Tihic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him and Sulejman Tihic was in that group that was flown away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know if Dragan Lukac was in that group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was in it, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you recall any other names of the men who were included in the group that was flown away in the helicopter?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the names of the others but I remember that the pilot of that helicopter was a young man whose name I don't know but the others had recognised him. He too had entered the gym where we were kept, and talked to the people he knew. Since he is much younger than I am, I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Where were you taken in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we got there, we stopped by the SUP building and then we continued on to the building of the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue your narrative. What happened upon your arrival at the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers were standing near the door of the bus. Soldiers who lived in villages around Samac. And they would beat everyone who was getting off. And they would ask everyone the same question, "And what have you done?" And they beat people without waiting for an answer. They put us up in the gym, and ordered us to empty our pockets and arrange anything that we had inside the pockets in front of ourselves. After a while, Stevan Todorovic came to the gym, gazed across the gym and then without looking at anyone in particular, he left. Several days later, we were moved to the building of the primary school, which is about a hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, give the Chamber an idea of how long it was that you were incarcerated in the primary school gym.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was locked up in the primary school building until the 4th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And the time remaining before the break, I'd like you to just give us a general -- give the Chamber a general picture of your treatment there. And then I'll later take to you specific episodes. First of all, were there beatings of the -- of both yourself and other prisoners in the primary school gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They beat people very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Again, frequency, please? Was this a daily occurrence, did a day ever go past without someone being beaten? And the frequency of beatings, please? How often they would occur, if they were daily?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes we would be beaten three or four times in 24 hours, especially during the night. Sometimes we would be beaten for days on end, without interruption. Sometimes there would be a couple of days' interval between beatings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Again I would like to you tell the Chamber if instruments were used? If so, what sort of instruments?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They used rifle butts, steel bars, wooden sticks, thick lengths of copper wire, truncheons, and according to some logic of our own, we fared the best when they used the truncheons because they inflicted the least injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Also, can you tell the Chamber of your assailants? You told us in the TO building they were mainly men of Serbian origin, that is from Serbia itself. But what about in the primary school gym, what sort of people were attacking you and the other prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers and policemen from Samac itself, and the environs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did civilians ever come into the primary school gym, local civilians?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honour pleases, I will have to move to specific episodes now. Would this be an appropriate time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We can have our break now and resume our proceedings at 1615 hours. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Examination-in-chief is continuing. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've given us a general description of the sort of attacks that you witnessed in the primary school gym. I'd like to now take you to specific episodes. Firstly, was a man you have already mentioned, Omer Nalic, in custody with you at the primary school gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you ever beaten with him? Together with him at the same time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It happened one night. They came into the gym. They ordered Omer to stand up. Stevan Todorovic's voice was heard. He ordered a soldier standing next to him to beat Omer Nalic. He beat Omer Nalic, and at the same time, Omer was begging him to stop, saying, "Stevo, why are you beating me? You know that I did nothing wrong." Then Stevan Todorovic said, "The guy next to him." He told me to stand up, I did, and then he hit me with a steel bar over the head. I fell down. I couldn't see because of all the blood that was flowing over my face. He told me to stand up. I couldn't. I didn't have the strength to get up. And then he pushed me in the chest with the steel bar and told me to grab it, that he would pull me up. I grabbed the steel bar and I was able to get up. Then he hit me again several times with the steel bar until I fainted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you recall what Omer Nalic was struck with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it was the same steel bar that was used to hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What sort of wounds did you suffer as a result of this attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had gaping wounds on my head. They bled for days, because the lacerations were quite wide and long and they could not heal for a long time. Later on, as the wounds healed -- actually, they were -- they became infected, the areas where I was hit on the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I take it you never received any medical treatment for -- following this particular attack or -- yes, following this particular attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know a man named Slavko Trivunovic? I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch your answer. And it has to be clear so that it can be recorded in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I do know Slavko Trivunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see him while you were incarcerated in the primary school gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A group of soldiers came in one evening, two of them took me out into the corridor and took me to the gym. They put me next to the entrance door. Two of them held my hands, standing at my side. One of them pulled me by the hair backwards and the other one opened my mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Before we get on to the details, I want this scene to be clear to everyone listening. First of all, were these group -- the group of soldiers, were they local -- local men, or were they from elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were from the area of Bosanski Samac and the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what about this man Slavko Trivunovic? What ethnic origin was he? And secondly, was he also from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's an ethnic Serb from a village in the vicinity of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Had you ever had anything to do with him prior to this encounter in the primary school?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know him. I had not known him. But later on some people told me what his name was, and what village he was from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like you to carry on with your narrative of what -- what happened to you? You got as far as telling the Chamber that two men held your hands, standing at your side, and one of them opened your mouth. Can you tell us if Slavko Trivunovic was there and then proceed with your account of these events?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavko Trivunovic was there. He approached me, laughing at my face, saying, "Now we'll make you more beautiful." Then I felt something metal against my teeth. I felt pain. And I felt my teeth crack. He kept putting metal pliers against my teeth. And sweeping them out. I was trying not to moan because I was standing at the door and my house was quite near. I felt the hot blood in my mouth, and since my head was bent backwards, I found it hard to breathe because of the blood, and Slavko Trivunovic continued putting those steel pliers into my mouth and kept pulling out my teeth. When he was done, the soldiers put me back into the gym. I was afraid I would faint. And I lay on my side in order to keep the blood flowing out of my mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How many teeth of yours were pulled out or cracked and damaged by this man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, I found a broken piece of mirror. I went to a corner of the room where nobody could see me. I opened my mouth and I looked. Three teeth had been pulled out from my lower jaw and in my upper jaw, two teeth had been pulled out. There was one tooth still standing. And then another tooth on the other side. So a total of six teeth. Other teeth that he had tried to pull out, I felt pain there, and as I felt with my finger, I could see that other teeth were -- were loose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you subsequently lose those teeth or did -- were you able -- do they, over time, fix themselves up, and were you able to keep them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lost three more teeth later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did this man, Slavko Trivunovic, have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His nickname was Harmonikas, the accordion player. That's what we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. called him in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did the guards have a nickname for him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you the only person to be attacked by this man in this fashion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you recall who else was subjected to this torture and how often it occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That evening, about a third of the men there had their teeth pulled out. While I was there, in the camp, I remember that occasion when people's teeth were pulled out. The next day, Slavko Trivunovic came into the gym. He had the dentist's pliers in his back pocket, and he asked if anyone needed their teeth fixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was he a guard at this primary school gym, as far as you're aware? Or was this episode just an occasion when he let himself in and availed himself of various victims?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a guard. Before the event and after the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You earlier testified that you know a man named Milan Simic. In the time that you were at the primary school gym, did you see him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He came one night. He stood in the middle of the room, and he asked us, he said, "Do you know that the president of the new Serbian government is here?" Then he left the room with his escort, and after that, they took some people out. We heard a lot of noise and moans.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's get a few more details. First of all, you say that he came into this -- into the room and made this announcement. Are you referring to the primary school gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He entered the primary school gym, among the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You say also that he then -- he made his announcement and he then left the room with his escort. What I want to know is, was that just one man or was he accompanied by a group? Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You say that he came at night. What was the lighting like at the time that he came in and made the announcement about being the president of the new Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no light, but the gym has large windows and I was able to see his face in profile in the moonlight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When he made the announcement, did you recognise his voice?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you say he left with his escort and then there was the sound of moans and so on. Can you just provide a little more detail on what precisely you did hear?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could hear the slamming of the doors to the gym. They got in and took out some of the prisoners, and you could hear the racket and the screams caused by pain, blows, again the doors opened, you could hear that, and people were thrown in and other people were taken out. And this was repeated, this whole scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time, that is that night, during the night, do you know who -- did you know then who was taken out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muhamed Bicic came to me in the morning and told me, "You can imagine, I was beaten by Milan Simic, and he visited my pizzeria so many times and I bought him drinks so many times."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did Muhamed Bicic bear any signs of a recent attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was from old wounds or new wounds. There were blood stains on his face, and I tried to wipe them off with a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you provide any comfort to him or try to provide any comfort to him other than trying to wipe off the blood with a piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained sitting next to him. I tried to give him some kind of psychological support to make it easier for him to forget that night and to instil some hope in him that we would be able to survive all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. I want to ask you if, during the period of time that you were incarcerated in the primary school gym, whether you received any visits from your wife?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife managed to have some sandwiches delivered to me and to the other prisoners I shared those sandwiches with. She did it through some of the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How often did this take place? How often would she successfully get food to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depended on who the guards on duty were. Sometimes she would manage to do that twice a week and sometimes once every fortnight. So it's really hard to say, that it was often. It was in fact quite seldom. But it did help us to survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In that time, were you able to see your children? In the time that you were at the primary school gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did anyone ever interfere or try to prevent your wife gaining access to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a corridor leading to the gym, and there was another small room which used to be a locker room, about two by two metres large, and there was a small window with bars. We were allowed to smoke in that room when we had cigarettes and we were able to look out. On one occasion, I saw Savo Cancarevic getting out of the car and threatening the guards, telling them not to let any women with food in. If they did not comply with that order, they would be held responsible. At that time, Savo Cancarevic was the police chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was there any sort of coherent system of shifts, as far as the guards were concerned? That is, would they change shifts at regular times, according to a regular pattern, or was it completely ad hoc and not capable of prediction?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not know when the shifts changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was that because there was no regularity as to when they would change?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards changed in the following way: Usually those who were on at night would remain until the morning, but -- and also they would change during the day, but I do not know the exact hours when they changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You've mentioned that your wife's delivery of food on -- helped you to survive. Can you tell the Chamber, other than what your wife gave you, the sort of rations that were being provided to the prisoners, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a time, it was quite difficult to subsist on the food rations that we received. We would be given a piece of bread, a spoonful of jam, and something that one could call tea, could pass for tea, and that's what we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How often were the prisoners fed? Perhaps I should clarify that. How often per day were the prisoners fed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So once a day they got a piece of bread a spoonful of jam and something that one might call tea? Is that a correct assessment of your food rations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long did that sort of -- how long were those sorts of rations provided to the prisoners, over what period of time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with any certainty, but it was a period of perhaps a month and a half. This was the period when we were given a piece of bread, spoonful of jam and a cup of tea.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Let me approach the issue this way. You were transferred to the primary school gym around the 13th of May, I think you said; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th of May, I arrived in Samac. First we were in the secondary school gym and then, after a day or two, we were transferred to the elementary school gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Were you exchanged and if so, what was the date of your exchange?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 4th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: For the last 15 days or so before your exchange, were you in the primary school gym or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was transferred once again to the TO building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm interested in the period of time between the 13th of May and the period of time from, say, mid-August, 1992. Now, during that time, you were basically in the primary school gym. The food that you received during that period of time, you've already described what you were receiving, marmalade -- a slice of bread, a bit of marmalade and tea once a day. Did that pattern change at all during the time that you were in the primary school gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you were eventually exchanged, had you lost weight?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was exchanged, I had lost about 30 kilos.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever see what the guards had to eat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see what they had to eat, but they looked quite normal, in terms of weight and appearance. I suppose they didn't lack food.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. You say that you were transferred for the last 15 days or so, before you were exchanged to the TO building, in that period of time, were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't beaten inside the TO building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In that last 15 days or so that -- when you were in the TO building, were you beaten anywhere at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown P49, please, and perhaps the B/C/S version as well, P49 ter ought to be provided to him. For the purposes of my examination-in-chief, I don't need the ELMO to be used but if the Defence want the B/C/S to be put on it, I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we should have it on the ELMO, the B/C/S. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I think you're familiar with this document, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Before April of 1992 -- yeah, April of 1992, were you the owner of a Zastava 101, which is a car?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I take it that in the Bosnia of April of 1992, there were in place systems of registration of motor vehicles?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Whereby the owner of a vehicle would register himself or provide information to the authorities, as the owner of a vehicle -- as being the owner of a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, you were married at that time to your wife, Snjezana. Thinking back to April of 1992, who was the registered -- the registered -- owner of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: This document purports to say that your vehicle, of which you are the registered owner, the Zastava was being requisitioned on behalf of the Bosanski Samac Crisis Staff. Did anyone ever approach you at the primary school gym and show you this document or inform thaw your car was going to be confiscated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When did you first lay eyes on this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Di Fazio, the document, I don't have the English translation obviously in front of me here but it was using the term requisitioned, was it not? You just used the term "confiscated." MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps I fell into error there. I perhaps should stick to the terms of the document itself. I'm glad that Your Honour has pointed that out to me. Yes. I'll make sure that that's pointed out to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, as Her Honour correctly pointed out the document says that your Zastava car was being requisitioned, not confiscated. That was my error, okay? But in the period of time that were you in the primary school gym, any time that you were in Bosanski Samac leading up to your exchange, did anyone from the Crisis Staff or a representative of the Crisis Staff come along and inform you, you, the registered owner of this vehicle, that was being requisitioned by the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what about on the actual day of your exchange? Was care taken to ensure that you received a copy of this document or that you were informed that your car had been requisitioned, before you left Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody gave me anything. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In fact, when did you first lay eyes on this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document after the exchange, when it was shown to me by my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Usher, I've finished with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'll come back to the topic of property in a while but now I want you to think about the -- your exchange on the 4th of September, and those events. You, I think, were incarcerated in the TO on the 4th of September when were you taken -- when you were finally exchanged?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get the complete translation on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'll ask the question again. I'll return to the topic of your property in a while but I want you to think now about the events of your exchange on the 4th of September. At the time, were you still incarcerated in the TO building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In the period of time that you were in custody, had you become aware of the phenomenon of exchanges? That is people, prisoners, being exchanged by both sides and whatever sides in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exchanges existed even before that date, and certain individuals who had been imprisoned with me had been exchanged before I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you hope to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about these exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: On the morning of the 4th of September, did you know that you were going to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the morning of the 4th of September, a policeman came and called out my name. He told me to follow him. We walked to the SUP building. In the hallway of that building, he told me to stop and wait for him there. I waited for half an hour while he went off somewhere. And then he came back and told me to follow him again. We got into a car and when we were inside the car, he told me, "You are going to be exchanged now."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Up until that point, had you had any idea that that was going to happen to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was afraid they were taking me again for interrogation at the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. But had you had any idea up until that time, that that was going to happen to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Had anyone consulted with you as to whether or not you wished to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed in your narrative about the exchange. You told us that you got to the SUP and got into the car with this policeman. Carry on from there, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we got into the car, the policeman told me that we were going for an exchange. He took me again to the gym of the primary school, and there was a number of people in the gym already. At that point, I asked another policeman if I could see my wife and children before the exchange. He replied, "They are coming with you." And that is when I learned that my wife and children are coming with me to be exchanged. They arrived half an hour later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. I want to -- the Trial Chamber to get a picture of the sort of people who were being assembled for this exchange. Obviously, there was at least one prisoner, that being you, and obviously, there were some civilians, that being your wife. Can you give us a breakdown of the other people who were assembled ready to be exchanged? Were some of them prisoners, some of them civilians?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several people who had been incarcerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Incarcerated with you in the primary school gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what about the civilians? Were there men, women and children? Young and old? Just give us a general picture.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
