utterances.text: There were old people, children and women among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What about their possessions? Was there any facility made for the transport of their possessions? Or was it just restricted to what they could carry?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife told me that they said one could take one travel bag of personal belongings, no electrical appliances, just footwear and clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You'd had your teeth pulled out, and I assume there were gaps in your teeth when you smiled -- in your mouth, I should say when you smiled. How did you feel about showing that to your wife?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the outset, I tried to cover my mouth with my hand, self-consciously, until she told me to stop doing that, and when she saw my mouth, I saw she was shocked, but we both tried hard to -- not to let the children see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And I take it everyone was loaded on to the buses and everyone took off and eventually you reached your destination in Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: During the trip, indeed at any point in the trip, did you see any of the defendants present?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you recall where you saw him? What he was doing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were stopped at Bosanska Gradiska, I could see, looking through the window, Miroslav Tadic sitting in an outdoor cafe, together with some other people. They were having refreshments. And I also saw him during the exchange itself. That was in Dragalici.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And is that in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Croatia, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me for one moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'd like to show the -- a portion of Exhibit P27 which shows the exchanges. It's a short portion of that particular videotape. It lasts in my estimation, about seven to eight minutes and I would like it to be shown together with transcript. The transcript, in fact, is Exhibit P27A and there was an addition to that a portion of the transcript that was added on which was the transcript of some German text, and it's been referred to, I know for sure, because I've checked the transcript and it was provided to the Chamber during the evidence of Dragan Lukic. I think it's just been made part of P27 but in fact they are two separate documents. P27A is -- contains the bulk of the transcript of the video and then I provided a little extra bit which was merely the -- merely the text, the German text. Now, I would hope that that's with the Chamber -- with the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, maybe she can check and find out what -- how many pieces of transcript she has.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, Registry has P27A, which is the English translation of P27A ter, which is the B/C/S version of P27, the exchange of prisoners. And as it was confirmed with the case manager this morning, the German bit is not included in this portion. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe it was not formally admitted into evidence. It might have been referred to. MR. DI FAZIO: I think that maybe that's happened. If that's the case, can I provide now a copy of the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't know if you want it simply to be added to P27A or whether you think we should give it a separate exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think because it's parts of the same video footage, isn't it? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it can have a slash, I think. It's a Prosecution -- so you can have P27A/1. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I've got several copies here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And P27A/1 ter. Since it's in German, I don't know whether we should use ter. MR. DI FAZIO: I can provide copies to the Defence if they don't have any handy at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have it just formally entered?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This extract, translation of the German text, will be P27A/1. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. And if Your Honours please, to assist you, you will see that the German text is -- consists of two paragraphs. At the top of the page, there is a paragraph that presumably comes in the videotape at the point 29.08.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: You will see that. That's to be -- if you want to follow it, you will have to follow it in P27A at page 13. If you turn to P27A and go to page 13, at the bottom of the page, you'll see text in German. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, that's where you would insert the first paragraph, 20, 2908. It says, "Text in German," and to follow the text in German, that's where it would be. 2908. Then if you continue turning over the pages of P27A, you get to page 15. About a third of the way down, do you see, "Text in German"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: And that would be the second part of the German text. And that would be from point 33.32 of the text. I hope that's clear. I would ask that the technical services people who already have the exhibit in the booth shortly begin to play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, I would like to you watch the video. MR. DI FAZIO: And Mr. Usher, can we make sure he can see it clearly on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And I'd just like you to watch the screen, carefully follow the text, as far as you can, and I'll ask you some questions about the people you can see in the text -- in the video. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If the technical booth could now start the video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The audio is very bad and the translation, too. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have interference. It's all right now. It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I just said that I'm going to show you a videotape and I'd like you to follow it. I may stop it from time to time and just ask you one or two short questions about the people depicted in the tape. Okay? MR. DI FAZIO: And if the technical people could now start running it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You were in the camp and what you were through, now we've heard you've lost about 40 kilos.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in several camps. I don't remember all of them. In Bosanski Samac, in Bijeljina, in Brcko. What can I tell you? I'm lucky to have come here alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How was it in the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Awful, beatings every day. They broke us, it wasn't simple beating. I don't know why they beat us so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. How many kilos have you lost?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly about 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did you get to eat or what didn't you get to eat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got a slice of bread, thinly spread with marmalade and a cup of tea. MR. DI FAZIO: Stop there, please. Would you just rewind it briefly, please? Slowly? Thank you. Just stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: First of all, the man who was speaking before, describing the loss of 30 kilograms and so on, do you recognise that chap?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's Muhamed Bicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was he exchanged on the same day as you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What about these two that you can see in the screen now? Do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man in blue is one of the Stjepanovic brothers, and next to him is a German citizen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. If you know the name of the German citizen, German gentleman, I'd ask you not to mention it in your evidence. We'll just Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. call him the German, okay? First of all, was he -- this German, was he ever incarcerate with you in -- well in any of the places you've described?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last 15 days before the exchange, in the TO building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was anyone able to communicate with him in the TO building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was with us, with the prisoners. When I was transferred from the elementary school gym he was already in the TO building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of any reason as to why this man had been incarcerated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He travelled from Germany to the town of Gradacac, which is 20 kilometres away from Samac. He had with him some goods for the textile factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, witness, you may not be able to follow the next portion of text because it may be in German but I'll just ask to you watch it briefly. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, you can follow the next portion of what the man says by reference to paragraph 2908 on the additional transcript. And with the technical services, may I ask them to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover]

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a German. He was in the camp. [German spoken, no interpretation] What can I say? It was horrible. MR. DI FAZIO: Can you stop there?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Again, was that the brother that you mentioned earlier, one of the Stjepanovic brothers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Could we continue, please

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac, in Brcko, in Bijeljina, and then again in Bosanski Samac. And we were beaten the worst in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did they use to beat you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything. That's all that I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you give a statement for the HTV?" MR. DI FAZIO: Can you stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover]

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please don't ask me anything I'm not in a position to speak. I don't feel like speaking anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Could you just -- MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who is that man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Had you had a hair cut before the exchange?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at the TO building, they cut our hair there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What about a shave? You look as if you've had a recent shave there. When did you shave before this exchange?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did shave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who gave you the clothes you're wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the clothes I had from before. And some pieces of clothing I had taken out of the bag that my wife had brought with her when she came to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: If the technical services people could please continue?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac. MR. DI FAZIO: Could the technical services people stop it there and just wind it back a bit now? Wind it back slowly? If you could keep on winding backwards, please? Okay. Stop it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who is the blonde woman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Stop it there, please, and just rewind it briefly. Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Now the gentleman with the beard holding the piece of paper, who is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who is that man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the Catholic priest from one of the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Had he been incarcerated with you in the primary school gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was incarcerated in the TO. So I spent the last 15 days of my imprisonment with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you remember what his name was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't recall it now. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you. In fact I think I'm done with the tape and I don't need to show it any more. Perhaps the technical services men can let the Registry have it back. If Your Honours please, I think I owe an apology to the interpreters. I had in fact prepared text to be given to them, but I realised when I got to this point in my examination-in-chief that I've mislaid it and brought it back so I'm grateful to them for interpreting on the spur of the moment, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I want to just return to a couple of issues that -- of your life in Bosanski Samac. First of all, the interrogations. You have already described one interrogation that took place in Bijeljina. Were you ever interrogated in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where was that and who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Bosanski Samac SUP. I don't remember the name of the police inspector who interrogated me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And was this during the period of time in which you were incarcerated in the primary school gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did they want to know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got there, he asked me if I knew why I had been imprisoned. I told him -- I repeated the thing that Stevan Todorovic told me when he arrested me. He then asked me if I was a member of the SDA, to which I replied that I was not. He went through some papers and told me that it was fine, that I was not on the list. Then he asked me whether I was a member of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia and when I left the party and that's all that I remember of the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: If you can tell us, please do. What I want to know is this: You say that he asked you if you knew why you had been imprisoned. Was this some sort of quiz, do you think? Or was that, in your view, a genuine question, he was that actually asking you what the reason was for your incarceration?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me, "Do you know why you had been imprisoned?" I said, "No, I don't know. The only thing I know is the thing that I was told by Stevan Todorovic at the time when I was arrested about what I had to be interrogated and the accusations that he levied against me at the time".

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he confirm that that was in fact the reason all of this had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In all those months that you were incarcerated in Bosanski Samac, in Brcko and Bijeljina and back there, did anyone, other than what Todorovic said, give you some sort of idea as to what it was that you had done to cause your imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: No document, to charge sheet, no formal sort of accusation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. I was never given anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Go back to the meeting in the SUP, and this interrogation. Were you asked to sign anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was giving my statement, a woman was typing, and they offered me this to sign immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you check the contents of what you were signing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was there any reason for your failure to do so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't dare to make any comments or to disagree with anything that was written there. I was under arrest, and I knew that any remarks that I might have made would have been to no avail.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You've described your -- the episode where your teeth were pulled. Can you tell us if you were interrogated after you had had your teeth pulled by Slavko Trivunovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Would your interrogator, whoever he was, have had an opportunity of seeing your missing teeth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And can you comment on the sort of condition that you were in during the course of this interrogation or this -- whatever it was? I'm thinking about now of your -- apart from your teeth and anything on your face and what your clothing looked like, those sorts of issues.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I had many scars and a couple of open wounds on my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your interrogator make any inquiry as to how those wounds came to be there? How it was that you were missing teeth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't ask me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you ever given a copy of this document that you signed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to turn briefly to the issue of your property. You've already described some of the property that you had, namely your car but I'd like to know a bit more about your home. Did you own the apartment that you were living in or have any sort of rights over that apartment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had the tenancy right of a house, an employee of my company lived on the first floor and I lived on the second floor, and in the attic, so I had the tenancy right to this apartment which had an area of 130 square metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: If all of these events that we have been talking about hadn't happened, and life had continued as normal, would you have been in a position to hand on this apartment to your children, in other words to provide them with an inheritance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can I ask you now to tell the Court what sort of personal property you had before April of 1992? I'm talking about household possessions, any machinery that you might have owned, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The apartment was fully furnished with all the appliances. In addition to that, I had built another building, a large garage, in my yard. And there I had various tools, a metal press, and a special sharpener, a machine for sharpening knives used in the paper industry. I also had some smaller welding machinery. I had stocks of sheet metal that could be used for further production. So this was an activity that I engaged in, in addition to my regular employment in the company where I worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Following your arrest, did you ever see any of that stuff again?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber what your wife took out with her in her bag on the day of your exchange?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She took some trousers, some shirts, and a jacket for me, some clothes for the children, and for herself, and most important of all for us, many of the photographs that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I asked you if any of the authorities in Bosanski Samac had said anything to you about your car that had been requisitioned at the time of your exchange. Was anything said to you at the time of your exchange, or subsequently, as to anything that you might do to recover this sort of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. property, the stuff that you'd kept in your garage, your personal household effects, that sort of stuff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't told anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Have you ever been back to Bosanski Samac since the 4th of September, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have never gone back since that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: On the night of the 16th of April, 1992, did you have any plans to leave your life in Bosnia and Bosanski Samac, any desire to do so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had no such plans. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a second just to prepare the earphones and the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Delic. Could you please tell me, you were a manager of the Mebos factory in Bosanski Samac before May, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the chairman of the board of management.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it's a position in the management?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there is a difference there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you could just make a pause of a few seconds between my question and your answer, because we speak roughly the same language. Do you accept that? So you were a manager, you had a position in the management?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat. I was the chairman of the board of management.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that you had a position in the management?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For a long time, you were a member -- you were in a managerial position in that company in the communist era; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the company from 1976.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, that was in the communist period, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by communism. Do you mean it was in the time when the Socialist Party was in government?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, this is a simple question, whether this was a period where the Communist Party was in power?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference between communism and socialism.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you had a managerial position in that company at the time where the Communist Party of Yugoslavia was in power, in a social system which was called socialism, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked there from 1976 and first I started working in the design office. Then I was in the manager of the production. And in the end, I became a member -- the chairman of the board of management.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, let me ask you this question again. Were you in a managerial position in the Mebos company at the time when, in the former Yugoslavia, the League of Communists of Yugoslavia was in power in a social system that is called socialism? I don't want to you get into your professional background. Could you please just answer my question with either yes or no? And then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the one-party system and I did work in Mebos.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: One party, yes, but which party? Could you please tell the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Socialist Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When was the Socialist Party established? MR. DI FAZIO: I object to the question if Your Honours please, and I should have objected earlier but I was trying to see where it was leading. I can see it's leading no where and therefore I object to the question. This witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You should wait. MR. DI FAZIO: This witness is not obliged to provide a history of the former Yugoslavia. He is here to give evidence of direct events of his experiences and what he saw and observed in Bosnia and Bosanski Samac at the relevant time. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Your Honours, I have not received the interpretation of the words spoken by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we -- maybe the interpreters have got it now. Can Mr. Di Fazio repeat the objection? MR. DI FAZIO: I'll do that. My objection, if Your Honours please, is this: This witness is not obliged to provide a history of the former Yugoslavia. His primary task is here to give evidence of what he saw and observed during the events of 1992 in Bosanski Samac. It is, with respect, completely irrelevant for him to provide a history lesson or to provide any sort of detailed political analysis of when the Socialist Party was formed and so on and so forth. For whatever reason, Mr. Pantelic thinks these relevant, then he can introduce evidence of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, I think we have heard enough about this question. What is important is that the witness has explained as to when he was employed in this company. So you may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, actually, that is the -- my question, and I'm waiting so much time, Your Honours, with this very simple questions. You were a witness that was nothing is in that and I was obliged actually to put ten or 15 questions for a very simple question because obviously this witness is mixing Socialist Party and Communist Party and I don't know how to proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: That is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. He is not. He's answering the question according to the way he understands it. In any case, what the Prosecution has said stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He is not here to give evidence on the political history of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It was not my intention at all, Your Honour. You will see with my next question that it was not my intention, but I unfortunately spent so much time to speaking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. Pantelic, I think the witness did almost at the outset stress that he began work at the Mebos company in 1976. So we have that, and if that's what you're interested in, we can just go from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact I'm not interested, it's just a corroborative moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Delic, was it possible for you, as a person in a managerial position in Mebos during the socialist regime, that you have your own privately run business? Is it possible or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it had been impossible, I would not have had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next question. This private workshop of yours, was it properly registered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you were paying taxes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you have employees?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you worked on your own after your normal working hours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked on Saturdays.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What did you produce in that workshop of yours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I produced metal-base plates for various -- for a farm, for a chicken farm, for a furniture production, production of chairs, tables and suchlike.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you sell those products at the company where you worked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your business partners who purchased those products that you produced, did they sell it to your company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I think we can have our break and resume at 18 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, because we are working until 7.00 today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We will have our break and resume our proceedings at 18 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, cross-examination continues, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before April, 1992, a rift started in Bosanski Samac among the three constituent nations, Serbs, Muslims and Croats; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There lived three constituent nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the period prior to April, 1992, specifically between October, 1991 and April of 1992, did those three ethnic groups live in harmony in the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally had a fine relationship with everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that the interrelations among the three ethnic groups had changed in any way as compared to ten years prior?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can I then conclude that your personal observations of the interrelations among the three ethnic groups, between October 1991 and April 1992 were that these groups lived in harmony and mutual tolerance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had good relations with everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand, as far as you are concerned, but in your every day life, while you moved around the town or when you occupied such a high position in the Mebos factory or in conversation with your friends, did you notice any internecine tension?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my company, and among the people I consorted with, I didn't notice any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You never heard anything about illegal arming?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You never noticed that Muslims frequented Muslim-owned cafes, Serbs frequented Serb-owned cafes and Croats went to Croat-owned cafes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you notice when Serb refugees from Vukovar to Samac in the end of 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice any refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you went together with other prisoners from the TO building to the Utva canteen for lunch, in your statement and during preparations for your testimony here, in some papers we got from the OTP, you said that Blagoje Simic was ten or 15 metres away from you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First you said that we spoke roughly the same language and then you used the term "when you went." We didn't go. We were driven under armed escort to the Utva factory. This distance here in the courtroom is a distance I consider to be ten or 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There were other prisoners around you, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was always in a group of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Blagoje Simic part of a group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two or three men standing along side Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So it would be logical to assume that he wasn't perhaps looking at you standing at that distance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said he was looking directly at me, directly at us, in fact, and specifically at me. He was facing us. He was looking at us and he was looking specifically at me. I have already stated this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But Blagoje Simic says that he never looked at you, and that he doesn't remember that scene, that event, at all.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comment to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you were transferred from Bijeljina in mid-May to Samac, you were first housed in the secondary school building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the gym of the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How long did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A day or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In that period, when Stiv Todorovic came there, who was he accompanied by?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say? You mean Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I mean Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came through the door alone. The guards were in the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Muhamed Bicic together in the gym with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Hasan Bicic there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a second, Your Honour. I have to check whether some of these names are protected. I don't want to be -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Was Ibrahim Salkic, nicknamed Ibela there in the gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had all arrived together on a bus from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. My question is, was Ibrahim Salkic, nicknamed Ibela, together with you in that gym during those three days, yes, no, or you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now we can go in private because I will mention the name of the Witness N.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are back into open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So did Stevan Todorovic show up at the secondary school only once in those couple of days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did Blagoje Simic come to the secondary school at any point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During your imprisonment in Samac, Samac was under shelling, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could hear explosions but we didn't know where.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You wrote a book titled "Be Brave and Forget Nothing"; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It speaks about the time of your imprisonment in Samac, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will read to you from page 75, written in your hand, chapter 18, titled, "Interrogation." I will read out one sentence. "For the umpteenth time this town is being shelled. When a shell exploded very close by, recently, I remained unusually calm." You did write this, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that part. I would have to look -- see the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just show the -- well, work in question, I would say, the book in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can show the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Delic, it's the last sentence on the right page, and it continues on the left page. Will you please look at the bottom of the right page? Highlighted in yellow. Can you see it? Is it exactly what I've just read?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an unofficial book. The official version of the book was published in one of the European countries in one of the European languages, and these are only drafts that I used to write this -- that book. This book was never published anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. So let us call them notes. In those notes that I read out, is it true what I read out about the shelling?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the only part you want the witness to answer. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe he was trying to correct the fact that that was not the actual book.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- to us whether in this draft he said that, yes or no, very simple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the witness can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As compared to this manuscript, the final version in one European language that was eventually published, underwent certain changes, and it is possible that those changes affected this particular part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. What counsel asked, whether you call it a manuscript for the time being maybe, it's a manuscript, he read a particular part of the manuscript, and all you have to say is whether or not that is the correct text in that manuscript. Not the truthfulness of what was stated, no, just what the counsel read to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If he could kindly read it once again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: "For the umpteenth time the town is being shelled. When a shell exploded very close by recently, I remained unusually calm."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm a little bit confused, Your Honours, because our learned friends provided us on the 1st of March with the short memo regarding the -- some minor errors in his language statement from January, 1995, inter alia on page 2. My learned friend, Mr. Di Fazio, mentioned that in this statement, second paragraph, related to his military service, now, during his -- I would say, preparation for this testimony, he said that he was not in military in 1997 but in -- sorry, that he was not in army in 1979 but in 1977. In his statement, he said that he was in army in 1979 and before this Trial Chamber he also testified that he was in army in 1979. In fact it is absolutely not of any importance, this issue, but still, due to the fact that we were provided with this memo from the Prosecution, I would like now to clarify that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead. Clarify with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Delic, in your statement made in 1995, you said that you served in the army in 1979 and you repeated the same thing here a couple of days ago; whereas, the Office of the Prosecutor made available to us a draft statement based on some interviews they had with you, where the year of your military service is stated as 1977. Which is the correct one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got married in 1979 so I couldn't have served in the army in the same year. I served in the army in 1977.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So when my colleague from the Prosecution asked you that question and you answered 1979, it was a mistake? It's nothing important, just for the sake of the record. You were in the army in 1977; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You are aware of the fact that in 1991, in the Posavina area, the Croatian community of Bosnian Posavina was established?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender into evidence two documents, ERN numbers are 00210327 and last two digits is 28 of the second document. Also I have a translation. The Prosecution was very kind to provide us with translation of this document. The document in question is actually certificate issued by Bosnian Posavina Croatian Defence Council for this witness and the members of his family. And I have a couple of questions with regard to that document and I would like that this document will be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, before they are tendered into evidence, can the witness look at the certificate and can you discuss it with him and see whether or not he knows anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. In fact it was provided by this witness to the Prosecution and it's a part of his statement from 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Does it have an English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I'm wondering whether the Prosecution know about this certificate? Or maybe they would like to have a look. MR. DI FAZIO: I think we do. I'm just trying to -- if Your Honours could just bear with me for a moment, I think I know what Mr. Pantelic is talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the meantime I have a sufficient number of copies. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. We are aware of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So first, we are dealing with the certificate dated 8 of September, 1992, issued by Croatian Posavina Croatian Defence Council for Fedja Delic and Almira Delic. These are the children of this witness, in fact. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm not concerned -- I'm not objecting. I'm just wondering if we could have translations. If Mr. Pantelic has any translations, if we could be supplied with translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a number, Your Honours, for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just want to be sure. Is it one sheet?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, just one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: On which all the certificates are contained? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, for this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please? As exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It will be D29/1 ter and D29/1 for the English translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, just put this English translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Delic, you have in front of you the certificate in your own language, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner, there is a heading, which reads, The Croatian Defence Council of Bosnian Posavina," isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about this institution?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Below that, it says, "The Crisis Staff of the Bosanski Samac municipality"; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about that institution?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, wait a minute. Did you know there was a Crisis Staff in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Below that, it is written, "Domaljevac headquarters."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is the distance between Domaljevac and Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You gave this certificate to the Prosecution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When were you given this certificate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand that you were given this certificate from the institution that issued it, and that is written up there in the upper left-hand corner, the Bosanska Posavina Croatian Defence Council, Bosanski Samac municipality Crisis Staff, Domaljevac headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody who was exchanged was issued with such a certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you given this certificate at the place where you were exchanged or when you arrived in Domaljevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went to Domaljevac after I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where did you go after your exchange?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Djakovo. That's in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you issued with this certificate in Djakovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were given this certificate after we were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In Djakovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber when after the exchange? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were about to board the buses, we were given the certificates. The certificates were already printed out and they just filled in the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you were given these certificates in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not in Bosanski Samac. In Croatia, after we were exchanged. After we crossed the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then you went to Djakovo with the certificate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind and read what it says on the stamp affixed to the certificate, if you could?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try. It says, "The Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about the small writing around the stamp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite difficult to read. I'll try as much as I can. "Croatian Community of Bosnian Posavina, Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." I think I read this right, because the writing is really small and it's not really legible. I hope that I got that right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please read what is written in the certificate after the handwritten word, "Bosanski Samac?" There is a comma after that. It begins with the words, "Was arrested."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please read it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Was arrested by the Serb or Chetnik aggressors in Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It is a term that is hostile towards the Serbian people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it is the way that Serbs see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How do you see it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Was arrested," I was arrested. "Serb or Chetnik aggressors," well, they were, those who made us sing Chetnik songs in prison. So they were in favour of Chetniks. If they made us, the prisoners, sing Chetnik songs. The aggressors, well, I have to agree with that, too. I would perhaps add also another term, the occupying force, and aggressor, because we were occupied by the Special Forces from Serbia and by the Yugoslav People's Army, and also by the local Serbs living in Samac and the environs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you agree that such terms should be used in an official document issued by an official body such as this one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is not sufficient, that you should also add the term, "Occupying force."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that such terminology, such wording, is used by the elements in Bosnia which do not want reconciliation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will not agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you think that such terms should be in normal circulation in Bosnia and Herzegovina? MR. DI FAZIO: I object to the question, if Your Honours please. It's difficult to see what relevance it would have, even if it were somehow narrowed down to perhaps time so that we know we are dealing with events in 1992. But it's hard to see what this witness's views about the use of such terms, how it could assist the Chamber. If Mr. Pantelic wants to put to this witness that he is a Croat or Muslim ultranationalist and so on and so forth and shouldn't be believed, that's fine, but I just don't see eliciting his views about the use of these terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. Delic, could you please explain to me and to the Trial Chamber, this is a stamp of the Crisis Staff of the Bosanski Samac municipality of the Croatian Community; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But that's not the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Samac in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please, have a look. What is your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But what do you conclude?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have to make any conclusions. I have no conclusions to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber how is it there are two municipalities of Bosanski Samac, one on the Croatian side and the other which in effect comprises the town where you lived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about that, because I wasn't the one who set it up that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. The next counsel who wishes to cross-examine? Yes, Mr. Pisarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Delic. My name is Borislav Pisarevic. I'm an attorney at law and I'm the Defence counsel for Mr. Simo Zaric. I will be asking you some questions, but before I do, I would like to express my deepest -- the deepest sympathies on behalf of my client for all the suffering that you and your family have been through in the course of this unfortunate conflict in the territory of our state, Bosnia and Herzegovina. So I wish to express his deepest regret. In the course of your testimony here, you explained to the Trial Chamber your links with and your involvement in the Party of Democratic Action in Bosanski Samac. Some things need to be clarified, however, and I would like to do so now, with your assistance. I hope that you will agree with me that the SDA, just as the SDS and the HDZ, is an ethnically based party, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You were on the SDA elections list at the elections held in 1991 and 1992 in Bosanski Samac. Do you remember, and can you confirm to this Trial Chamber the fact that the leader of the list, the person that was at the top of the list, was Mr. Sulejman Tihic, who was at the time the president of the municipal board of the SDA party for Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see the list myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to your testimony, you were on the list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that I was on the list, and that I was not listed as an independent or separate candidate of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that by dint of appearing on the SDA elections list, that you supported the platform of the Party of Democratic Action in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a non-party candidate or independent candidate, I was in a position to support a part of the platform of the SDA party, and the part that I'm referring to is the one that favoured the independent Bosnia and Herzegovina and one vote for each person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, can we make one thing clear? I'm talking about the platform for the municipality of Bosanski Samac, not the general state-level policy of the SDA. Are we clear about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the SDA list but before that, we had discussed my being a non-party candidate, and yet that was not done in that way. This was not done by the SDA but as Sulejman Tihic explained to me, by other parties who refused to allow a distinction between SDA party candidates and non-party candidates that ran under the SDA umbrella.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, you will agree with me that the elections were conducted by the municipal electoral commission and that they determined the conditions and all the other elements that were necessary for these elections to be carried out in accordance with the law of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the statute of the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably am not aware of the electoral procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please confirm for me the fact that the manager of the Mebos factory in Bosanski Samac was Zvonko Prce?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please confirm that he was a Croat, an ethnic Croat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the Mebos company, in the division of posts among the parties that won the power, that it was assigned to the HDZ party?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the managers in companies were appointed in accordance with the agreement reached by the parties in government in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In those companies where not much work was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Delic, I still do not want to elicit your opinions. I may want to do so later but can you please just tell me whether you are aware of that fact or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard some rumours to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned a meeting at the local commune, which you attended. Do you know who organised the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber who notified you of the meeting and of the agenda of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sulejman Tihic informed me that a meeting would be held and that the issue of the opening of the bridge would be discussed at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, were there other managers of other companies present at the meeting? I mean companies from Bosanski Samac. Or were you the only one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that all the three ruling parties in Bosanski Samac were represented at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall who attended the meeting on behalf of the Democratic Action Party?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that [redacted] [redacted], also attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was this meeting chaired by [redacted]

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember because I was late for the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in addition to the issue of the bridge, that there were some other issues on the agenda, issues related to the security in the town of Bosanski Samac and so on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because I left the meeting after the topic of the bridge was discussed, because that was the only thing that I was interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So I can conclude that you did not remain at the meeting until its end; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the bridge on the River Sava connecting the Republic of Croatia and the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was under the jurisdiction of the municipality of Samac and the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and not of the local commune of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with these legal matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that at the time, the bridge on the Sava River would be closed very often?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct. And the company where I worked had problems because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the bridge over the Sava River on the Republic of Croatia side was guarded by the National Guards Corps and by the army of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, in which period?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In this period, precisely.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never crossed the bridge in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did perhaps the drivers from your company or some other people who travelled that way tell you anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hold any meetings with the drivers about that, and I did not receive any information to this effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone report to you or did they report to you why they were unable to cross the Sava River at Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was a problem, they would just tell me the most -- the bridge is closed and we have problems bringing in or taking out the production materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at that time, the bridge was closed quite often by the Croatian army and the members of the ZNG, the National Guards Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear from anyone that the bridge had been mined, booby trapped on the Croatian side, that mines had been laid down there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: But you do know the fact that on the side of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the bridge over the Sava River was guarded by police officers of the Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who guarded the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when a unit of the Republican Ministry of the Interior came to Bosanski Samac from Sarajevo and that this unit guarded the bridge on the Sava River connecting the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell me how did this meeting end, or rather this item pertaining to the opening of the bridge over the River Sava connecting the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina with the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I left, I urged them to find a solution, and after the discussion and the interventions, I understood that the bridge would be guarded and that it would be opened for traffic. That was enough for me, and I left the meeting very happy and satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. At that meeting, you also took part in the discussion and so did Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN HASANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that it is time for us to break, and as I'm about to embark upon another topic, perhaps this would really be a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We can adjourn the proceedings to tomorrow afternoon at 1415 hours. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, if Your Honours please, I wonder if Defence counsel could give us an indication of approximately how much longer they will be so we can organise our next witness? I think we probably coming to the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic, how much more time do you think you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, not more than 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. And then Mr. Lukic, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that my cross-examination will also take about ten minutes, but perhaps I will come up with some other topics during the night. But I think that's more or less the amount of time that I'm going to need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Baen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Probably about 15 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think you can work your arithmetic Mr. Di Fazio. We will rise now until tomorrow. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Ms. Reidy, you wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and sorry for delaying us here, it's just that that's a time for the cross, but could I just get any indication from the Bench whether they are expecting any break for legal submissions between these witnesses or should we just continue with the next witness? I know there is the outstanding matter of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. We did agree that after this witness if we are going to continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So we would agree just on Ms. Baen's response on the witness issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Right now, I can't say whether or not we will continue that far, because as you can see, Judge Singh is not here, so we will be able to know finally tomorrow so we will just dealt with the possibility of completing re-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Of course, if we have to continue, it will be -- we shall deal with Variant A and B before the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Court will rise.
